sources.entry: Nova - The beautiful, fast, flexible, native Mac code editor from Panic.

summary.name: Nova
summary.one_liner: Nova is a native Mac code editor from Panic with a built-in terminal, Git, remote file transfers, debugging, and a JavaScript extensions API.
use_cases: editing code natively on a Mac
developing Rust, Swift, or C/C++ projects
editing and publishing files on remote servers
committing and pushing Git changes in one app
building custom editor extensions in JavaScript
summary.what_it_does: Nova is a code editor built with native Mac frameworks, offering an editor with features such as minimap, multiple cursors, and per-language settings for indentation and display. It combines editor, terminal, and Git in one workspace, with clone, fetch, pull, commit, and push support and sign-in to GitLab and GitHub. It can browse, edit, and publish files directly on remote servers. It includes a debugging sidebar with breakpoints and console debugging, plus build/run/clean tasks triggered by toolbar buttons or shortcuts. Its extensions API uses JavaScript and includes templates, and it supports language servers that Nova can install.
notable: Native Mac app built with native frameworks for low memory use and battery life
Extensions written in JavaScript with built-in templates
Live previews that update as you edit, with WYSIWYG-style web editing
Remote file transfer and publishing directly within the editor
caveats: Free 30-day trial, with paid licensing implied after the trial but not detailed on the page
